chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-A'la ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who slaughters and does not say (Bismillah). He said: If he had forgotten, there is no problem, provided that he was a Muslim and was skilled at slaughtering, and does not pierce the spinal cord, and does not cut off the neck after having slaughtered.

key_terms.لا بأس: No problem, no objection; formula indicating permissibility
key_terms.ناسياً: Forgetful; one who forgot to perform an obligatory act
key_terms.يسمي: Naming, i.e., saying 'Bismillah' at the moment of slaughter
key_terms.يقطع الرقبة: To cut off the neck completely; prohibited before the animal dies
key_terms.ينخع: To pierce or sever the nasal/spinal cord (nakh'); a prohibited act in slaughter

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a Muslim forgets to say Bismillah when slaughtering?
ai.summary: Muhammad ibn Muslim narrates his question to Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) about the permissibility of meat from an animal slaughtered without the invocation of Bismillah. The Imam rules that it is permissible if the slaughterer forgot to say it, provided three conditions are met: he is a Muslim, he is competent in the proper method of slaughter, and he does not perform the prohibited acts of nakh' (severing the spinal cord) or cutting off the head before the animal is fully dead. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that forgetfulness (nisyan) can excuse an omission, while deliberate abandonment would render the meat impermissible.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the man who slaughters and does not Name (Bismillah). Heasws said: ‘If he had forgotten it, so there is no problem when he was a Muslim, and was good at slaughtering, and did not flip it over nor cut off the neck (until) after having slaughtered’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who slaughters but does not mention the name of Allah. He (the Imam) said, ‘If it is because of forgetfulness, it is not unlawful if he is a Muslim, knows slaughtering properly, and does not cut off the spinal cord and the neck after slaughtering.’”
